title: Nutrition and Transport in Flowering Plants
seo_title: Secondary 3 Biology: Nutrition and Transport in Flowering Plants Worksheets (O-Level)
standard_code: O-Level Biology (6093): Nutrition and Transport in Flowering Plants
standard_text: Describe the structure of a dicotyledonous leaf and how it is adapted for photosynthesis; state the word and chemical equations for photosynthesis; describe the role of chlorophyll; investigate the need for light, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll and the effects of limiting factors; state the importance of nitrate and magnesium ions; describe the uptake of water by root hair cells, the movement of water through the xylem and transpiration and the factors affecting it; describe wilting and the translocation of sucrose and amino acids in the phloem (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Biology worksheets on nutrition and transport in flowering plants: leaf structure, photosynthesis, limiting factors, xylem, phloem, transpiration and potometers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Leaves make glucose; xylem brings water; phloem carries sugar.
key_sub: Transpiration is fastest when warm, dry, windy and bright.
body_html:
How to think about it

A leaf is a factory for glucose.

  • Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.
  • The rate is limited by the factor in shortest supply: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration or temperature.
  • Xylem carries water and mineral ions up from the roots; phloem carries sucrose and amino acids (translocation).
  • Water evaporates from the mesophyll and diffuses out through the stomata: transpiration pulls water up the xylem.
Example

Bubble moves 6 cm in 3 min. Rate?

6 ÷ 3

Answer: 2 cm/min

Example

Lamp from 10 cm to 20 cm. Light?

intensity ∝ 1/d²

(10/20)² = 1/4

Answer: 1/4 as much

Common mistakes

  • Saying plants get their food from the soil.
  • Mixing up xylem (water) and phloem (sugar).
  • Saying transpiration is faster in humid air.
  • Halving the light intensity when the distance doubles (it falls to a quarter).

faq.q: What are the limiting factors of photosynthesis?
faq.a: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature. The factor in the shortest supply limits the rate.

faq.q: What is the difference between xylem and phloem?
faq.a: Xylem vessels are dead, lignified tubes that carry water and mineral ions up from the roots. Phloem is living tissue that carries sucrose and amino acids to all parts of the plant.

faq.q: What affects the rate of transpiration?
faq.a: It is faster at higher temperature, lower humidity, higher wind speed and higher light intensity (when the stomata are open).

items.q: Why must ethanol never be heated over a flame?
